card_title: A signal sent from your mitochondria
card_summary: Rendered from a content record only, to test the cell energy template.
headline: A message your mitochondria *send out*.
lede: Most of what mitochondria do stays inside the cell. MOTS-c is different: a small peptide your mitochondria make that appears to travel and act elsewhere. Almost all of what we know comes from lab and animal work.
recognition: You've kept moving and you still notice it: workouts land differently than they did, and your body seems to respond to effort on a slower clock.
reframe: MOTS-c gets attention because exercise appears to raise it, and because in animals it acts on the same energy-sensing switch that exercise flips. Whether giving it to people does anything comparable hasn't been tested in a published trial.
viz_intro: MOTS-c is coded in your mitochondria's own DNA. It leaves the mitochondrion and, in lab studies, switches on an energy sensor in the cell.
viz_alt: A mitochondrion on the left sends gold dots along a dotted path to a cell nucleus on the right, showing MOTS-c traveling as a signal.
viz_molecule_label: Gold dots: MOTS-c on the move

viz_nodes.node_detail: MOTS-c is coded by a short stretch of mitochondrial DNA inside a gene called 12S. It's 16 amino acids long.
In cells and mice, MOTS-c switched on AMPK, an energy sensor, and cells used more sugar and fat. Under stress it moved into the nucleus.

viz_caption: Simplified, and based on lab and animal research.
viz_tap_hint: Tap a plum dot for detail.
gauge_title: Muscle MOTS-c, before and after one workout

gauge_states.state_note: Baseline levels in muscle before exercise.
In 10 young men after one cycling session, muscle MOTS-c rose about 12-fold. Blood levels rose about 1.5-fold.

gauge_scale_note: Roughly to scale for muscle. A small study in men only.
mechanism_title: What we know, and what we don't
mechanism_intro: Most rungs here sit low on the evidence ladder.

mechanism_steps.step_body: Your mitochondria carry their own small set of DNA. MOTS-c is one of the few peptides made from it.

mechanism_steps.step_title: In animals, it acts on an energy switch
mechanism_steps.step_body: In mice, MOTS-c switched on AMPK and changed how the body used sugar and fat.
In one small study of young men, a single workout raised MOTS-c in muscle and, more modestly, in blood.
In men, blood MOTS-c was lower with age while muscle MOTS-c was higher. There isn't a clean story here yet.

mechanism_steps.step_title: No published human trials of MOTS-c itself
mechanism_steps.step_body: A modified version was tested in a small early trial, with results shared only in a company press release.
